messages.subject: histograms for transition frequencies by type stochastic mapping
parts:
Dear Nick

Great tools. I had been playing with phytools stochastic mapping, and liking it, so this is great. One thing I liked was his tool for estimating the evolutionary time spent in each state.  Hint. 

Is there a way I could produce histograms like you show at link below, but for each node? Even if that doesn't make sense, can you give me a clue as to how I produce those histograms? Which table or tables contain the information? What are the object elements I should use?

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script#hist_BSMs

Also can you give me a hint about how to avoid doing the time stratified analysis? The example seems to default to that. My data is attached....in case you have some pointers.

Sincerely

Chris Buddenhagen

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] histograms for transition frequencies by type stochastic mapping
parts:
Hi Chris,

The outputs are in the script, they are:

clado_events_tables
ana_events_tables

There has been some discussion on the Google Group about how to read the tables, the function prt() etc. will help.  Parsing these tables would get you to residence times in each state pretty easily, or events by node.

Re: stratified, it should pretty much run if you switch the input to being an object from a non-strat analysis:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script#BSM_script
===============
Notes:

This is a time-stratified DEC+J analysis. To run other models, or a non-time-stratified model you will have to edit the model setup; see the setups of 6 basic models in the main BioGeoBEARS example script.
As usual, you will have to change the script to specify your own working directory.
The input files (in this case, for a time-stratified analysis of Psychotria, with Hawaiian islands disappearing back in time) should auto-load from the BioGeoBEARS extdata directories specified. Change these directory locations/file names to use your own files.
Also, if you switch to a non-stratified analysis, be sure to change stratified=FALSE to stratified=TRUE.
===============

I have half a tutorial done but I won't be able to get back to it for awhile as, as my advisors say, I have to focus on overdue publications and projects (and hopefully soon-ish, a stochastic mapping publication) -- rather than tutorials which (speaking frankly!) won't get me a job in the future.  Advisors say I can put in serious time for collaborations of course, so that's the best way to get help with things that take substantial time, that are beyond what exists in the example scripts.

Cheers!
Nick
